descriptions.text: Upgrade Patch. Medium. Ah, yes. The Midnight Epicure. The Caprid Who Devours the Sky. This scary-ass fable is used to terrify children across the universe. […] Over the cycles, the rather disturbing symbol of the Midnight Epicure, which is really just a racist caricature of an adult Caprid, developed into a ward against all night evils. If this upgrade patch is affixed to an eligible garment, it will imbue the following upgrades: Protection against Vampirism. Protection against Lycanthropy. +25% Magical damage against all sapient undead. Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

beats.headline: The Plenty's goat
beats.text: Carl's gold box from the Plenty hisses, spins and opens like a flower on a patch for his jacket, the same size as his white bomb patch: black, denim-like material with a gray goat head screen-printed on it. Donut mutters about screen printing. Read the description, says Mordecai, and sew it on right away. Carl has seen the satanic goat before, on the back of Prepotente's hand, and sketched it into the cookbook, assuming it was a deity's mark. The description calls it a fable. Its benefits are exactly those of the silver bracelet Donut has just pulled from her own box.

beats.headline: Sewn on, not straight
beats.text: Mordecai suggests letting Miriam Dom die and collecting her gear in the morning: two sponsors who know more than Carl have just spent a fortune protecting him from vampirism, and a vampire is asking for help the moment the sun sets. She saved my life, says Carl, grabbing the sewing kit; if it is a trap, they will be protected. He sews the patch on beside the bomb patch, his wide stitches covering Katia's careful threading, and Donut gasps that it is not straight. It is good enough. An achievement, a few levels in sewing, and the patch glows as it is officially affixed.

beats.headline: Protected by the jacket
beats.text: Carl stabs the loose heart of the boss in the rain, and the monster explodes, showering gore over all of them and spilling the rest of itself from the ruined trees. When Mongo leans down to bite at the remains, Carl tells him not to dare. Vampirism is contagious, and Carl knows that if his jacket did not protect him he would likely be infected: he would die, then wake up overcome with hunger. Half the dinosaurs in the forest are infected already.

beats.headline: She can see the glow
beats.text: Carl is still cautious with Miriam Dom, and she understands why. The two of them are in no danger from her, she tells him. She can see the glow on them: Carl and Donut are both protected from vampirism, and she could not feed on them even if she wanted to.

beats.headline: The goat is a god
beats.text: Carl asks Prepotente about his god; all he knows of it is what the patch on his jacket says, the one that protects him from vampires and werewolves. The Midnight Epicure, says Prepotente, protects all prey animals by destroying all existence after unleashing all the consumed back into the galaxy: they who were eaten become the devourers. It began as a xenophobic tale to scare non-caprid children and grew into a symbol of hope and comfort for his kind. His sponsors gave him the ability to worship it in a benefactor box.
